title: The Ever-Evolving World of Science

standard_code: Class 7, Curiosity Chapter 1: The Ever-Evolving World of Science
standard_text: Science as a process that keeps growing and changing with new evidence; observation, questions, hypotheses, experiments, analysis and conclusions; contributions of scientists including those from India; scientific attitude and evidence versus belief (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 1).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 7 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 1: the scientific method, evidence, how scientific ideas change, Indian scientists and a scientific attitude. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Scientific ideas change when new evidence is found.

body_html:
How to think about it

Science is not a fixed list of facts. Scientists observe, ask questions, form a hypothesis, test it with experiments, analyse the results and draw conclusions. When new evidence appears, ideas are tested again and improved, as when the idea that the Sun goes round the Earth was replaced.

New instruments such as the telescope and the microscope opened new worlds. A scientific attitude means being curious, open-minded and asking for evidence, so we can tell tested claims from superstitions.

Example

'A black cat brings bad luck.' Is there evidence?

it has never been shown by fair tests

Answer: no: it is a superstition

Example

Keeping nails in salt water and plain water for a week is…

a fair test

Answer: an experiment

Common mistakes

  • Thinking scientific ideas never change.
  • Treating a popular belief as evidence.
  • Changing results to fit a hypothesis.

items.q: Which of these is not a claim supported by evidence?
c: The plant kept in light grew taller in our measurements.
Ten repeated trials gave almost the same result.
The thermometer showed that the water boiled at 100 °C.
Wearing a lucky shirt helps you score more marks.
items.e: “Wearing a lucky shirt helps you score more marks.”: not a claim supported by evidence. The other three are.

items.q: Which instrument helped Galileo see the moons of Jupiter?
items.e: This showed that not everything goes round the Earth.

items.q: Why is it important to question even well-known ideas?
c: testing them again can reveal mistakes or improve them
because all old ideas are wrong
items.e: Asking 'how do we know?' is the heart of science.

items.e: “Our graph shows that the pendulum's time does not depend on the mass of the bob.”: not a superstition. The other three are.
